# Kestle Bay heat pump programme: board meeting notes, 14 November 2024

## Kestle Bay heat pump programme: board meeting notes, 14 November 2024

Present: Rosa Penhallow (chair), Daniel Kitto, Meera Joshi, Tom Rowe and Ellen Vosper (programme manager). Apologies: Gareth Lobb.

## Progress

Ellen reported that the first phase closed in September with 214 installations. Installers now report a median of 9 weeks between the home survey and the installation date, down from 14 weeks in the first year of the programme.

## Installers

Brightwater Heating withdrew from the programme in August because of staff shortages, leaving Pellow and Sons as the only appointed installer. The board agreed to run a new tender in January to appoint at least one more installer before phase two begins.

## Complaints

Six formal complaints were received in 2024, four of them about installation delays and two about the condition of gardens after outdoor units were fitted. All have been resolved.

## Phase two

The board agreed a target of 150 further installations by March 2026, with priority for homes heated by oil or bottled gas. It also agreed to cap the householder contribution at GBP 4,000 for households receiving means-tested benefits, with the society's hardship fund meeting the rest of the cost.

## Actions

Ellen to draft the installer tender by 12 December. Daniel to ask the Coastal Communities Net Zero Fund whether the grant can stay at GBP 6,000 per home in phase two. Meera to update the website with the new waiting times.

  p.1: "Evaluation of the Kestle Bay Community Heat Pump Programme, 2022 to 2024" #BGNKDZBYBQ
  p.1 §Abstract: "Kestle Bay Community Energy, a community benefit society, ran a programme between October 2022 and September 2024 to help owner-occupiers on the Kestle Bay peninsula replace fossil-fuel heating with air-source heat pumps." #9ANETYPCPM
  p.2 §1 Introduction: "Kestle Bay Community Energy set out to tackle these barriers locally. It recruited households through village halls and word of mouth, arranged free home surveys, negotiated a group price with two installers and administered a grant funded by the Coastal Communities Net Zero Fund. This report evaluates the programme's uptake, its effects on energy bills, indoor temperatures and emissions, and residents' experience of their new heating systems." #YT837X4S9V
  p.3 §3.2 Data sources: "Temperature loggers were placed in the living rooms of 48 homes that volunteered, recording every thirty minutes for one winter before and one winter after installation." #D9FS2TCVMS
  p.4 §3.5 Resident survey and temperatures: "The follow-up survey asked about comfort, running costs, problems and overall satisfaction, and was sent to all households with an installation. Temperatures were summarised as the mean living-room temperature between 1 December and 28 February in each winter." #12B5RDS34X
  p.4 §4.1 Uptake: "Between October 2022 and September 2024, 597 households registered an interest, 318 received a home survey and 214 had a heat pump installed." #C5TRV3RGNG
  p.6 §4.3 Indoor temperatures: "In the 48 homes with temperature loggers, the mean living-room temperature from December to February rose by 1.6 deg C, from 17.9 deg C before installation to 19.5 deg C after. This gain was largest in homes that had relied on electric storage heaters, which had often been the coldest before the programme. Fewer residents reported shutting off rooms in winter to save money. The comparison is not adjusted for weather, and the second winter was on average 1.1 deg C milder outdoors than the first." #Z6KXV7GQEH
  p.7 §4.5 Residents' experience: "Among respondents, 84 percent were satisfied or very satisfied with their heat pump, and 77 percent said their home was more comfortable than before. Twenty-three households, 11 percent of those with an installation, reported a fault in the first year (Table 3). Most faults were fixed within a week, but three households were without heating for more than five days." #JXKNQVMW56
  p.8 §6 Limitations: "There was no comparison group of homes that kept their old heating, so changes in bills and temperatures may partly reflect other changes in households. Meter data were complete for only 162 of the 214 homes, and temperature loggers were placed in only 48 volunteer homes, which may not be typical." #A7CC4DWHXD
  p.8 §7 Conclusions: "The Kestle Bay programme shows that a community energy group can deliver heat pumps at scale in an area with many older and off-grid homes." #YVW5FY11NW

  p.1 Borrowing instead of buying: evaluation of the Brackenford Library of Things pilot, April 2023 to March 2025
  p.1 Northfold Social Research, for Brackenford Libraries. Final report, September 2025.
  p.1 The Brackenford Library of Things lends household tools and equipment from three branch libraries for a small fee. This report evaluates the first two years of the pilot, from April 2023 to March 2025, using membership and loan records, a survey of borrowers and the checks that staff make when items are returned. Almost 2,000 residents registered as borrowers, and loans grew by 64 percent between the first and second years. Borrowers reported modest savings, and most items came back in good condition. Registrations from deprived neighbourhoods were roughly in line with their share of the town's population. We recommend that the scheme continues, with changes to how damage is recorded and how new items are chosen.
  p.1 Libraries of things apply the familiar library model to objects that households need only occasionally, such as drills, gazebos and sewing machines. Their supporters argue that borrowing saves money, reduces the number of rarely used items that people buy, and brings people into libraries who would not otherwise visit.
  p.1 Brackenford Libraries opened its Library of Things in April 2023 with a grant of GBP 96,000 from the Halden Foundation, which also funded this evaluation. The pilot ran from three of the town's seven branch libraries: Central, Eastgate and Millbrook.
  p.2 Items could be reserved online and collected from any of the three branches, and loans lasted up to seven days.
